status: pre-registered 25 Nov 2026, before any of its runs started. Written AFTER every study_v2 result had been seen, session 2 included. Logged in deviations.json. Later changes go to a 'deviations' list in this file with what had been seen.
kind: exploratory follow-up of study_v2 (sensitivity analysis of history length); does not change study_v2's choice.json, A0 or families F1-F3
question: With one fixed, already tuned network, how does session-2 accuracy change with the length of history the model sees: reset windows of 0.5-10 s and carried-state chunks of 0.5-10 s?
seen_at_registration: all study_v2 results, session 2 included; the 2 s reset window was screened in study_v2 R1 only (did not clearly lose to 1 s); 5 s and 10 s reset windows were never run; carried state was tuned at 2, 5 and 10 s chunks.
design: no tuning: every arm takes a reference config unchanged except its length (reset: 'window'; carried state: 'chunk'). The configs are not re-tuned per length, so a length that would want other settings is under-rated; this is a limitation, not corrected.

reset.config: study_v2's 0.5 s full-overlap winner TS2_R2_w50_full_f3: 64 units, 1 layer, dropout 0.004, lr 0.00556, batch 64

carry.config: A0 = study_v2's 2 s carried-state winner TS2_R1_carry_2s_d5: 64 units, 1 layer, dropout 0.017, lr 0.00754

reused_runs.w50: seeds 10-12 from FE_cell_w50_full (same changes); 13-14 run as FE_win_w50
reused_runs.carry200: seeds 10-12 from FE_cell_carry_2s, 13-14 from FE_A0 (same changes); nothing new is run

spec_ids: FE_win_<arm>; windows: the reference's changes with 'window' set; carried state: with 'chunk' set (window stays 20)
order: longest first (w1000, w500, w200, w100, then carried state, then w50), so the slowest arms are not the last to start

WS1.what: reset windows vs the 0.5 s window

WS2.what: carried-state chunks vs the 2 s chunk (A0)

WS3.what: reset window vs carried state at the same length

metric: study_v2's: session-2 nMAE per person, median over the 5 seeds
decision_rule: study_v2's: per comparison, an effect counts only if all 6 people agree in sign and the median effect is at least 5 %; otherwise 'no clear difference'. Each comparison is scored on the samples both of its arms predict (from max(1 s, the later first prediction of the two arms)), so a 10 s window is compared only on samples from 10 s into a trial on.
descriptive: session-2 nMAE against length for both sweeps on one shared start (the latest first prediction of any arm)
fixed vs tuned config at 5 s and 10 s carried state (FE_cell_carry_5s, FE_cell_carry_10s, seeds 10-12); at 1 s reset (FE_cell_w100_full)
run time and weight updates per arm
relation_to_followup_carry_chunks: followup_carry_chunks.json (19 Nov) asks about chunks of 1, 0.5 and 0.2 s with full tuning. WS2 gives a fixed-config answer for 1 and 0.5 s; the follow-up is not replaced and stays as registered.

budget.estimate: about 83 h from study_v2 run times scaled with window length (reset finals 33 min at 0.5 s and 51 min at 1 s; 2-10 s extrapolated; carried state about 17 min at any chunk); the first 10 s runs are measured before the estimate is relied on

paused: fine_round_2 (5 of 234 runs finished) is paused while this runs and resumes after it
limitations: Chosen after seeing every study_v2 result, session 2 included: exploratory, never reported as part of study_v2's pre-registered comparisons.
One config per sweep, tuned at 0.5 s (reset) or 2 s (carried state); other lengths are not tuned.
Long windows are scored on fewer samples per trial (from 10 s on for the 10 s window).
